subject: Nimbus per-token pricing schedule - swingpoints & clawback options
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus per-token proposal: swingpoints & clawback options

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per follow-up, attaching a short proposal and an example cost workbook that shows how per-token economics look across three commit shapes. High level: we want to keep the hosted API pricing usage-based, but make the contract simple to operate for your finance and procurement teams. The two constructs we laid out are: 1) breakpoint-triggered marginal pricing (per-breakpoint marginal rate after each volume threshold), and 2) an averaged/true-up model where the effective rate is blended over the entire billed period (simpler invoicing).

Quick ask: which construct does your procurement/legal team prefer as a default? If neither, we can propose a hybrid (blended baseline + marginal overage).

Attached: Nimbus_PRICING_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf (short narrative + table), nimbus_cost_examples_Q3.xlsx (model).

Suggested next steps:
- Elaine: confirm preferred construct (marginal vs blended) and any must-have billing constraints by Fri 9/17
- Redwood: provide a clean redline with both options and a sample invoice extract by Mon 9/20

I summarized two sample numbers in the attachment but called out the main tradeoffs: marginal gives clearer unit economics at scale but increases month-to-month invoice volatility; blended is predictable for accounting but can obscure marginal incentives and requires a true-up cadence.

Thanks — any questions ping me or Ben.

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Attachment: Nimbus_PRICING_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf (1.2MB), nimbus_cost_examples_Q3.xlsx (43KB)

From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus per-token proposal: swingpoints & clawback options

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear deck and the model. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Procurement prefers the blended/true-up approach for simplicity; our AP team would like a single effective rate per billing period if possible.
- Legal flagged two items: (a) a one-quarter true-up window (we prefer not to have retroactive credits older than 90 days), and (b) we need a short clawback clause if committed volumes are not met over a rolling 12-month period.
- Can you show an example invoice that demonstrates how a blended rate would look for 3M, 10M, and 30M tokens per month? The workbook helps but AP wants a sample line-item extract.

If Redwood can provide a blended bill-with-true-up option and the 90-day cap on retro credits, we can move to commercial redlines next week.

—
Elaine
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nimbus Health
elaine.wu@nimbushealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus per-token proposal: swingpoints & clawback options

Nice capture, Soojin — and great feedback from Elaine. A negotiation play we should consider (recommendation): offer the blended/true-up as the default (to satisfy AP), but include an optional marginal overage schedule that only kicks in above the top committed tier (e.g., >30M tokens/month) for aggressive volume economics. That preserves a predictable invoice for the customer while giving them cost incentives as they scale.

Key points for the commercial redline:
- Blended baseline with quarterly true-up; credit retro limited to 90 days (matches their ask)
- Overage marginal schedule above top tier with clear attenuation (so there aren't step shocks)
- No retroactive clawback for previously invoiced periods beyond the 90-day window; instead a rolling adjustment on future invoices

I'll draft the commercial language and a sample invoice extract. Marissa can prep the example invoice lines using the workbook. Marcus — can you weigh in on whether we should add a soft cap on aggregate liability in the clawback language?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus per-token proposal: swingpoints & clawback options

Quick read — agree with Ben's hybrid approach. A couple of legal/finance cautions: 

1) Clawback math needs to be deterministic and capped. Suggest language: "clawback credits limited to 15% of the annual committed spend, applied within a 90-day true-up window." That prevents runaway risk.
2) If we include marginal overage tiers above 30M, avoid abrupt percentage changes; use a smoothing factor or multi-step attenuation (e.g., 30–60M: -7%, 60–120M: -5%) to avoid stepwise billing surprises.
3) Require that any invoice samples we provide are explicitly non-binding and labeled as "example invoice".

If legal/procurement at Nimbus accepts those constraints, we should be able to move to redlines. Marissa — LMK if you need specifics for the sample invoice layout.

Marcus Lin
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
